SHA-256 hex digest (C backend)

Source: R/core.R
csha256.Rd

Computes the SHA-256 hash (FIPS 180-4) of text or raw bytes with the self-contained implementation in the package's compiled core, and returns it as a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal string. A hash is a short fingerprint: any change to the input changes it, so it is used throughout the package to record exactly which data, mapping or file a result came from. Sibling packages use the same routine through LinkingTo: rmoriebricklayer.

Usage

csha256(x)

Arguments

x

A character vector, or a raw vector. Other atomic vectors are converted with as.character().

Value

A character vector of 64-character lowercase hex digests: one per element for character input, length 1 for raw input (character(0) for an empty character vector).

Details

For a raw vector the bytes are hashed as one message and one digest is returned. Any other input is converted with as.character() and each element is hashed separately, as the bytes of the string as stored in memory (no re-encoding). In a UTF-8 session those are the UTF-8 bytes; for a string marked latin1 they are the latin1 bytes, so use enc2utf8() first when the digest must be the same on every platform. NA gives NA. Numbers are hashed through their printed form (1 hashes as "1"), and a factor through its labels.

For a digest of a whole R object, hash its serialization (see the examples) or use dgstobj; for BLAKE2b use cblake2b.

References

National Institute of Standards and Technology (2015). Secure Hash Standard (SHS). FIPS PUB 180-4. doi:10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4

Examples

# Hash a character scalar (NIST test vector for "abc").
csha256("abc")
#> [1] "ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad"
# ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad

# Vectorised over character input: one digest per element.
csha256(c("abc", "def", NA))
#> [1] "ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad"
#> [2] "cb8379ac2098aa165029e3938a51da0bcecfc008fd6795f401178647f96c5b34"
#> [3] NA                                                                

# Raw input hashes the bytes directly; identical to the character form.
identical(csha256("abc"), csha256(charToRaw("abc")))
#> [1] TRUE

# The empty message.
csha256(raw(0))
#> [1] "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"

# Fingerprint an arbitrary object via its serialization.
csha256(serialize(list(a = 1L, b = "x"), NULL))
#> [1] "5d31430add6fdb81ad2d63cc9b82953ee454b281238856418d0bb6ca232afbc7"
